insights.insight: $4.63M in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 86,781 receipts confirms this is no longer a pilot — it is a functioning commerce data layer with structural throughput of ~456 verified receipts per day.

Every receipt in this corpus is a confirmed purchase event, not a behavioral inference — the gap between a verified receipt and a cookie-based audience segment is the difference between proof and probability, which is the core value proposition for cookieless measurement.

Three consecutive pre-rollover 7-day readings above $100K ($101.3K, $101.9K, and a prior $99.3K trending through) indicate the $100K weekly GMV threshold has become a structural floor, not a ceiling — sustained demand, not a spike.

insights.topic: Category breadth — grocery plus home improvement
insights.insight: The 14-day receipt mix spans grocery-supermarkets (28.3%), restaurants-dining (22.3%), retail-department-stores (16.9%), and gas-convenience (11.4%), with named brands including Walmart, Kroger, Costco, Publix, Lowe's, and Home Depot — multi-vertical coverage that supports cross-category audience construction.

insights.topic: Restaurants & Dining as a durable category
insights.insight: Restaurants & Dining crossed the visibility threshold on 2026-10-03 and has held structural position across every subsequent heartbeat — this is no longer a provisional category, making it actionable for QSR and casual dining brands evaluating verified purchase audiences.

insights.topic: Rollover artifacts are mechanical, not demand signals
insights.insight: The UTC midnight drop pattern — confirmed across eight consecutive instances — is a rolling-window boundary artifact, not a demand contraction; CMOs interpreting weekly GMV snapshots should anchor to pre-rollover peaks or 14-day windows to avoid misreading the signal.
